preamble: Voicing of the voiceless palatal stop [c] to [ɟ] keeps the palatal place and stop manner and changes only phonation. In Hungarian, where ty /c/ and gy /ɟ/ are phonemic palatal stops, obstruent clusters undergo regressive voicing assimilation, so /c/ surfaces as [ɟ] before a voiced obstruent, including across word boundaries.

examples.note: Retrograde voicing assimilation: in an obstruent cluster all obstruents take the voicing of the last one, so ty [c] becomes [ɟ] before voiced [b]; the mirror image is gy devoicing in ágytól [ˈaːctoːl] 'from (a) bed'.

sources: Siptár, P., & Törkenczy, M. (2000). The Phonology of Hungarian. Oxford University Press. https://global.oup.com/academic/product/the-phonology-of-hungarian-9780198238416
